about: The RBI FREE-AI committee report's 26 recommendations (six pillars) assessed against what the estate demonstrably does. Recommendations addressed to the RBI, the government or the industry are marked not applicable; those the board owns are entity duties and never counted as covered. The report is guidance from a committee, not a binding direction. Titles are paraphrased; the notes are our own assessment and can be wrong: challenge them.

source.title: RBI, Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of Artificial Intelligence (FREE-AI), committee report
source.caveat: Recommendation titles paraphrased from a professional summary of the report (the RBI's PDF could not be fetched from here); numbering is per pillar, not the report's own. Confirm against the RBI's text before relying on it. Status is our own judgement.

items.title: A board-approved AI policy
items.note: The board approves the policy. The estate supplies what the policy points to: the inventory, the approval tiers, the stop switch and the incident runbooks.

items.title: Data lifecycle governance for data used in AI
items.note: Classification-aware routing keeps local data off cloud models, personal data is redacted, and stored data has limits and tiers; there is no record of which data sources feed which knowledge base.
items.next: A lineage record: each knowledge base and the sources it was built from, with owner and class (doc 105, G15).

items.title: AI system governance across the model lifecycle
items.note: Every model has a risk tier, owner, approval, validation date and decommission record; weights must match an approved digest; any model or all AI can be stopped at once.

items.title: AI-specific risk checks in product approval
items.note: High-risk models need named approvers and evidence (threat model, red-team scorecard, DPIA) in the registry, and the inventory flags an unapproved model; no sign-off checklist is generated for the product committee.
items.next: A product-approval checklist generated from the registry, signed by the committee.

items.title: Consumer protection: transparency, fairness and grievance redress
items.note: Answers say they come from AI; grievance redress is the entity's; there are no bias or fairness probes yet.
items.next: Bias and toxicity probes in the purple loop (doc 105, G5); a disclosure line the entity can set per channel.

items.title: Cybersecurity against AI-specific threats, and AI for detection
items.note: Input and output rails against injection, leakage and exfiltration, proven by the red team; the AI-SOC triages alerts.

items.title: Regular red teaming of AI systems
items.note: The red team runs in the purple loop and scores four of the ten OWASP LLM categories.
items.next: Every OWASP LLM and Agentic category, plus bias probes (doc 105, G5).

items.title: AI contingencies in the business continuity plan
items.note: An AI outage is a continuity scenario with its steps; a failed provider falls back to the next rung and the local model.

items.title: AI incident reporting and sector risk intelligence
items.note: AI incident runbooks start the right reporting clocks and keep sealed evidence; the sector-wide AI incident repository is the RBI's to set up, so no channel to it exists yet.
items.next: Add the sector AI incident channel to the regulators once the RBI names it.

items.title: An AI inventory, and a contribution to a sector repository
items.note: ./securax ai inventory lists every model with tier, owner and validation due, and checks it against what the gateway actually serves.

items.title: Risk-based internal and third-party audits of AI
items.note: A hash-chained gateway log, a checksummed evidence pack and these machine-checked maps give an auditor something to test; the audit itself is the entity's.
items.next: An auditor's export of the AI controls with their evidence, in one file.

items.title: AI governance and use disclosed in annual reports
items.note: The entity discloses. The inventory and the board report give the numbers.

items.title: A standard AI compliance toolkit
items.note: Addressed to the RBI, the government or the industry, not to a regulated entity's own estate. For one entity, ./securax comply and ./securax readiness do this job.
